correctness.rationale: Four exact cyclic moments parameterize the six observations. The derivative moments yield exactly two nonnegative leading-modulus roots; outside explicit null strata the mixed moment inverts uniquely for the constant coefficient. The false-branch energy discrepancy is a nonzero real quadratic polynomial with value three quarters of the difference between four times the leading-coefficient energy and the middle-coefficient energy at zero, hence its zero locus has measure zero. A polynomial-map rank argument excludes fewer than three roots; the integer noninjectivity pair is exact. The proof and standalone script verify the crucial identities without treating finite tests as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Section 3.1 and Question 3.5 of arXiv:2205.08753v1 give the exact 2022 motivation, all-signal five-point sufficiency, four-point counterexample and open almost-everywhere threshold. A separate 2019 paper proves generic-array, rather than fixed-array, sufficiency. The new two-branch reconstruction proves sharp almost-everywhere recovery from three fixed cube-root samples, with an exact exceptional witness. Repeated semantic and bibliographic searches found no implication or stronger matching classification; unindexed work is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Semantic and bibliographic indexing is not exhaustive: a later unindexed or unpublished proof of the same fixed-array result remains possible.
No claim is made about degenerate coefficient strata, higher degrees, or numerical conditioning.

value.rationale: This is a sharp answer for the smallest genuinely quadratic case of the published derivative-magnitude sampling Question 3.5. The explicit two-branch inverse and nontrivial ambiguous pair separate generic from all-signal phase retrieval and reduce that case from five to three roots per channel with a rigorous minimality proof. The solved invariant is the natural smallest sampling mesh, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
